items.title: Third IIT Bombay suicide this year puts student pressure under spotlight
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A Dalit B.Tech student at the Department of Energy Sciences and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT-B) died by suicide on Friday, September 18, in what is the third such suicide this year at the campus. 19-year-old Sahil Wakode from Maharashtra’s Yavatmal district was accused of using his phone to cheat in the midterm exam conducted on Friday. He was found unresponsive in his room at Hostel No. 4 on the campus by hostelmates later in the evening. The campus has since erupted in demonstrations by students, with an impromptu protest occurring upon the discovery of the body and carrying on through the night. A protest call was given on the morning of September 19, and students assembled at the site in the face of police barricades. Sahil’s parents reached the campus on September 19, demanding a CID probe into their son's death and alleging caste-based discrimination at the institution as having played a major role. “My son has been tortured. items.title: Warangal airport land acquired, CM Revanth Reddy asks public to suggest names
items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy announced that the land acquisition for the long-pending Warangal airport has been fully completed and handed over to the Airports Authority of India (AAI). He invited suggestions from the public on what to name the new airport in Warangal’s Mamnoor. Union Minister for Civil Aviation K Rammohan Naidu had previously said that the airport could be completed in 30 months once the state government handed over the required land to AAI. On September 14, AAI floated a tender worth Rs 213.59 crore for the development of the Warangal airport, with works including construction of a new domestic terminal building, an Air Traffic Control Tower cum Technical Block, Fire Station, and other associated works. “This is not just an airport. It is a new gateway for industry, tourism, education, jobs and investment,” CM Revanth said. Telangana currently has only one operational airport, the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) in Hyderabad. The Mamnoor airport in Warangal has remained defunct for decades and attempts to revive it have been ongoing for years since the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) was in power.
